Risk Management Plan
Yuba City Wholesale, Grow West
Yuba City, California

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 

ES-1.0  FACILITY ACCIDENTAL RELEASE POLICY
The owners, management, and employees of Grow West | Yuba City Wholesale (herein referred to as the Yuba City Facility or Facility) at 2100 Everglade Road, Yuba City, California 95993 are committed to the prevention of any accidental release of anhydrous ammonia, aqua ammonia, or regulated pesticides. Grow West has prepared this Risk Management Plan (RMP) in accordance with the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA) regulations to address process and operational safety. 

If an accidental release were to occur, the Facility is prepared to work with the local fire department, or other authorities, to mitigate the release and to minimize the impact of the release on people and the environment. A detailed Emergency Response Program (ERP) has been developed and will be implemented in the event of an accidental release. 

ES2.0	FACILITY INFORMATION
The Yuba City Facility provides fertilizers and related products to farmers and other agricultural supply operations. The Facilitys primary activity is the sale of liquid fertilizers, including anhydrous ammonia and aqua ammonia; granular fertilizers (prill); and a variety of non bulk, pre packaged chemicals (e.g., herbicides and pesticides) to farmers in the Sacramento Valley of Northern California. The applicable NAICS code for this facility is 42491 (Farm Supplies Merchant Wholesalers). The Yuba City Facility is not co-located within one mile of another regulated facility and has not had a reportable accident within the last five years. No practicability assessment for inherently safer technology or design (IST/ISD) is required. The Facility does not have an NAICS code that requires compliance with Process Safety Management (PSM). 

The Yuba City Facility has been assigned the U.S. EPA Facility Identifier number 1000 0020 6207 and has a physical address of 2100 Everglade Road

Yuba City, California 95993.

ANHYDROUS AMMONIA 
  The maximum amount of anhydrous ammonia in inventory exceeds the U.S. EPA regulatory threshold of 10,000 lbs.
 
  Anhydrous ammonia is a liquefied, compressed gas that is shipped in U.S. Department of Transport (DOT) / Motor Carrier Compliance (MCC) code 331 specification tanker and offloaded into on-site pressure vessels (a.k.a., bullets). 

  Anhydrous ammonia (NH3) is received, stored, and converted to aqueous ammonia, or distributed in nurse tanks for direct application as crop production nutrient. 

  Anhydrous ammonia, as a liquefied compressed gas, will boil under ambient atmospheric conditions. Liquid ammonia will expand by 850 times when it evaporates. 

  The anhydrous ammonia is offloaded from the delivery vehicles and pumped into either the 15,000 gallon storage tank or the 18,000 gallon storage tank. 

  The anhydrous ammonia storage vessels are filled to no more than 85% of shell volume. 

  Nurse tanks are filled to order and immediately transported offsite to be delivered to the client. The Nurse tanks are not used as stationary storage. 

  The DOT nurse tanks are returned empty from client sites. The empty nurse tanks may contain a de minimis amount of ammonia present (effectively empty) and are not considered part of the inventory. 

  The maximum quantity of anhydrous ammonia handled is 144,177 pounds.

ES3.0	ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM
The Facility has implemented the following prevention program elements.

* Process Safety Information (PL3) | Safety Information (PL2).  
The Facility confirms that information concerning covered processes and regulated substances is up-to-date and available for review by employees. Safety Information includes Safety Data Sheets (SDSs), chemical inventories, operating limits (temperatures, pressures, flows, compositions), equipment specifications, and Codes and Standards used to design, build, and operate the process. For PL3, the information includes block flow and piping and instrument diagrams (P&IDs) (where applicable), descriptions of safety systems, and materials of construction information for the installed systems. 

* Process Hazards Analysis (PL3) | Hazard Review (PL2).  
A review of the ammonia processes is conducted every five years or as needed following a process change. A revie

w of the results from the most recent hazard review for the anhydrous ammonia process, aqua ammonia process, and pesticide handling and storage indicates that no high-risk hazards were identified by the review team.

*Operating Procedures.  
Written operating procedures have been developed for the covered processes. The operating procedures for the anhydrous ammonia are reviewed and recertified on an annual basis. The operating procedures for the aqua ammonia and the regulated pesticide are reviewed, updated, as necessary to reflect current practice, or whenever the tasks or steps to perform on the covered process are found to be inadequate or inaccurate. 

*Training.  
Facility personnel and Grow West corporate management understand that incidents involving the accidental release of regulated substances can be reduced by having adequately trained operations and maintenance (O&M) personnel. A training program, which incorporates operating procedures and safe work practices, is an essential element of an effective prevention program. 

The current training program is comprised of the following:
  Initial employee training.
  Periodic refresher training.
  Training provided for new equipment additions or modifications.
  Competency testing involving written tests and observation following training; and
  Training records for each employee.

*Mechanical Integrity (PL3) | Maintenance (PL2). 
The Yuba City Facility has implemented a Mechanical Integrity / Maintenance program for its regulated substances. The program at the Facility is intended to preserve the mechanical integrity of the process equipment to minimize the potential for an accidental release. The program includes equipment inspection, preventive maintenance, recordkeeping, and training and is conducted in accordance with manufacturers requirements and industry practices (e.g., Recognized and Generally Accepted Good Engineering Practices, RAGAGEP). 

*Management Of Change (PL3).  
Operational, safety,

and environmental issues must be reviewed prior to the initiation of a process change to ensure that they do not compromise the safety and integrity of the Anhydrous Ammonia Process, and to minimize adverse effects to worker safety and public health. The Management of Change (MOC) procedures are used to evaluate changes to process materials, controls, equipment, and procedures.

*Pre-Startup Safety Review (PL3).  
The pre-startup safety review (PSSR) applies to additions or modifications to the Anhydrous Ammonia Process that require the safety information to be revised or updated. As changes in affected processes are identified or planned, they must be evaluated and a PSSR completed if deemed necessary in accordance with operating procedures. The assessment is undertaken in conjunction with the MOC review. A PSSR is performed in conjunction with the MOC review process when the proposed change requires modifications to the safety or operational procedures.

*Compliance Audits.  
Grow West conducts triennial compliance audits of the RMP program to assess the effectiveness of the written plan and to identify gaps in the program. Records of the audits and follow-up documentation are maintained to indicate findings and resolution of findings. 

*Incident Investigation.   
Although no incidents involving regulated substances have occurred at the Facility in the last five years, Grow West has an incident investigation program and documentation in place. The program includes investigation requirements and reporting and would be implemented in the event of an incident.

*Employee Participation (PL3).  
The Facility must rely upon the operational expertise and training of its employees at all levels and disciplines to ensure safe operations. The Facility has an Employee Participation Program in place and has implemented procedures regarding engaging employees for their input, providing access to safety documentation, and seeking employee knowledge and experience in applicable

areas of the program. 

*Hot Work Permit (PL3).  
For hot work that may occur on or near the Anhydrous Ammonia Process, Grow West has developed a written Hot Work Permit program and procedure to document the requirements to complete the work and provide adequate fire prevention and process protection. 

*Contractor Safety (PL3).  
The contractors used by the Facility for anhydrous ammonia services have been informed regarding the known potential fire, explosion, or toxic release hazards related to anhydrous ammonia at the Facility. The Facility qualifies contractors who are engaged in maintaining the Regulated Substance (RS) systems to ensure that equipment is properly repaired and returned to service safely.

*Other Code Applicability.  
The Facility implements the provisions of the following guidelines, regulations, and standards for these regulated substances (partial list):

Regulated Substances
  California Code of Regulations, Title 19 [Public Safety], Division 5, [California Environmental Protection Agency], Chapter 1 [Hazardous Materials Inventory and Response Plans].
  California Code of Regulations, Title 19 [Public Safety], Division 5, [California EPA], Chapter 2 [California Accidental Release Prevention Program Detailed Analysis].
  United States Department of Labor, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), 29 CFR 1910.38, Employee emergency response plan and fire prevention plans. 
  United States Environmental Protection Agency (U.S. EPA), 40 CFR Chapter I, Subchapter C, Part 68, Chemical Accident Prevention Provisions.

Anhydrous Ammonia
  United States Department of Labor, Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA), 29 CFR 1910.111, Storage and Handling of Anhydrous Ammonia.
  California Code of Regulations, Title 8, Division 1, Chapter 4, Subchapter 1, Unfired Pressure Vessel Safety Orders, Articles 2 and 6.
  Compressed Gas Association (CGA) Requirements for Storage and Handling of Anhydrous Ammonia, CGA 2.1-2023 .

Anhydrous Ammonia and Aqua Ammonia
  American Society of Mechanical Engineers, 31.3 Process Piping.
  California Fire Code, Chapter 50, Hazardous Materials.

ES4.0	FIVE-YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY
There have been no accidental releases of anhydrous ammonia, aqua ammonia, or regulated pesticides during the last five years resulting in death, injuries, evacuations, shelter in-place orders, or property or environmental damage.

ES5.0	THE EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM
The Facility developed an Emergency Response Program (ERP) in accordance with the requirements presented in the RMP (and CalARP regulations Section 5120.2). The Emergency Response Program is developed in accordance with Title 19, Division 5, Chapter 1, Article 3, Section 5030.9 Emergency Response Plans and Procedures. The ERP will be implemented in the event of an accidental release of a regulated substance. 

ES6.0	PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY
Safety is integral to the operations at the Yuba City Facility. Implementing safety improvements is an on-going process at the Facility. Grow West conducts periodic evaluations to assess the effectiveness of the maintenance and safety programs. Specific changes to the anhydrous ammonia, aqua ammonia, and regulated pesticide processes at the Facility will be implemented as needed.

ES7.0	THE WORST-CASE RELEASE AND ALTERNATIVE RELEASE SCENARIOS
The Yuba City Facility prepared off-site consequence analyses (OCA) for the three processes at the facility. The OCAs evaluated the Worst-Case Release Scenario (as defined in regulation) and an Alternative Release Scenario (i.e., the more likely condition). 

*Anhydrous Ammonia.  
The worst-case release scenario is the failure of the largest storage tank when filled to the greatest amount. The largest single tank currently in inventory is the 18,000-gallon storage tank, filled to 85% volume. The storage tank holds a maximum of 78,642 pounds (15,300 gallons) of anhydrous ammonia. A catastrophic tank failure would result in a d

istance to the toxic endpoint of 2.12 miles. For the alternative release scenario, identified by Grow West during the process hazards analysis (PHA), is a release from a 2 inch pipe which lasts 2 minutes. That release would have a distance to the toxic endpoint of 1.18 miles. 

*Aqua Ammonia.  
The worst-case release scenario for aqua ammonia is the failure of the largest storage tank when filled to 219,500 gallons. The 1,668,200 pound release of aqua ammonia solution (equivalent to 406,075 pounds of NH3) to the secondary containment. This WCS would have a distance to toxic endpoint of 0.35 miles. The alternative release scenario is a release from a broken 2-inch diameter pipe to the truck load-out containment pad totaling 10,000 lbs (~1,315 gallons). That release would have a distance to toxic endpoint of 0.14 miles.
